ai.title: Add shell shims for direct agent command invocation
ai.summary: New `codebuff shims` subsystem enables direct command execution of agents without the `codebuff` prefix via generated shell scripts. Implementation spans `npm-app/src/shell-dispatcher.ts` for cross-platform shim generation (Unix/Windows) and `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/shims.ts` for CLI logic. Supported subcommands include install, uninstall, list, update, doctor, upgrade, and env. Shims are stored in `CONFIG_DIR/shims` and rely on fully qualified agent IDs (`publisher/agent-id@version`).

eli5.text: You can now save a helper as its own app command. After running a setup command, you can type that helper's name directly instead of opening a separate program and asking for it. The setup works on Windows, Mac, and Linux, installs the helper into your settings folder, and gives you commands to add, remove, update, check, upgrade, or list your installed direct commands.

ai.title: Fix runIdToStepAll key in runProgrammaticStep
ai.summary: Corrects the `runIdToStepAll` set key from `agentId` to `runId` in `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts`. This aligns the tracking mechanism with the actual execution context, ensuring `STEP_ALL` commands are correctly associated with the specific run rather than the broader agent state. Internal fix to backend logic; no user-facing API or UI changes.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a task that applies to everything in a single session, it was previously tagging that action using a broad identifier that could mix up which session it belonged to. This correction makes sure the action is tied to the exact session it ran in, so tracking and logs stay accurate for internal debugging. There are no visible changes to how you use the product.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.492 ships shell shims, run-scoped programmatic steps
ai.summary: Freebuff 1.0.492 rolls up same-day work across the monorepo: a new `codebuff shims` subsystem in `npm-app/src/shell-dispatcher.ts` and `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/shims.ts` generates shell scripts for direct agent invocation without the `codebuff` prefix, stored in `CONFIG_DIR/shims` and keyed by fully qualified agent IDs like `publisher/agent-id@version`; the same release corrects `runIdToStepAll` keying in `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts` from `agentId` to `runId` so `STEP_ALL` tracking is scoped per run, adds `runId` to the `AgentState` type in `agent-definition.ts`, and updates programmatic step caching and QuickJS sandbox keys in `quickjs-sandbox.ts` accordingly. On the SDK side, `@codebuff/sdk` now outputs both ESM (`dist/index.mjs`) and CJS (`dist/index.cjs`) bundles with `package.json` `type: module` and conditional `exports` mapping `import` to ESM and `require` to CJS, adds `ws` 8.18.0 to runtime dependencies in `sdk/package.json`, and ships `sdk/README.md` API key URL and example clarifications; SDK v0.2.1 also relaxed custom tool generic constraints from `Record<string, unknown>` to `any` and corrected the Zod import to `import { z } from 'zod/v4'`, while the
ai.evidence: The diff shows a single version bump in `npm-app/release/package.json` from 1.0.491 to 1.0.492. The commit is a release-bump with +1/-1 stat, and release instructions indicate the version number change itself should not be described; instead, the surrounding same-day commits provide the user-visible content.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.492 adds the ability to run your favorite agents directly from your terminal without typing the full command prefix, plus it introduces a brand-new lightweight AI agent that uses the fast Grok 4 model for quick research and code review tasks. The command-line now installs small shortcut scripts (called shell shims) so you can start an agent with a simple, short name instead of a long publisher/agent path, and you can manage those shortcuts with commands to list, update, doctor, or remove them. The web agent store also got faster and smoother: the long list of agents now scrolls smoothly thanks to virtualization, the store page refreshes agent data in the background instead of reloading everything, and the login and onboarding screens work better on phones and tablets. Other improvements include fixing broken links in the documentation, making the SDK client correctly handle running commands in the right folder, and ensuring agent conversations stay complete instead of getting cut off on the server side. Upgrading gives you quicker access to agents from your terminal, a snappier web store experience, and more reliable agent runs with fewer glitches and better error handling.

ai.title: SDK dual ESM and CJS build support
ai.summary: SDK build now outputs both ESM (`dist/index.mjs`) and CJS (`dist/index.cjs`) bundles. `package.json` updated to `type: module` with conditional `exports` mapping `import` to ESM and `require` to CJS. New compatibility tests added for both module systems.

eli5.text: The helper kit that other software uses to talk to Codebuff can now be loaded in two different ways: one for modern projects and one for older projects. If you're building something that uses Codebuff's tools, your project can now choose whichever style of importing it you normally use, and it will work without conversion steps. The two separate packages are built side by side, with the modern one being the default for new projects. If you looked, you'd see two different bundle files in the output folder, one labeled for modern style and one for older style.

ai.title: Fix custom tool types in SDK v0.2.1
ai.summary: SDK v0.2.1 fixes type definitions for custom tools by relaxing generic constraints from `Record<string, unknown>` to `any` and correcting the Zod import to `import { z } from 'zod/v4'`. This change addresses type errors preventing valid tool definitions from compiling. The update affects `sdk/src/custom-tool.ts` and bumps the package version in `sdk/package.json`.

eli5.text: Custom tools in the developer toolkit used to throw type errors that blocked valid tool definitions from compiling. The toolkit now relaxes those strict type checks and corrects how its data-validation library is imported, so custom tool definitions compile cleanly again. This affects developers building custom tools on top of the toolkit (SDK consumers), who would have previously hit compilation errors when defining tools whose input shapes didn't match the overly restrictive types. The fix is live today in the newly published toolkit version.

ai.title: Disable researcher-codebase-explorer subagent
ai.summary: The researcher-codebase-explorer subagent is disabled in the researcher-grok-4-fast definition. It was removed from the spawnableAgents list and references in the instructions prompt were updated to reflect its absence. Additionally, the researcher-codebase-explorer definition itself was updated to explicitly restrict terminal commands to read-only operations, likely a preparatory step or safety hardening even if currently disabled.

eli5.text: The research assistant that scans code has been temporarily turned off because it was slowing things down; when it runs, it will now only use read-only commands. If you're using the fast research pipeline, it will no longer spawn the code-scanning helper, and the remaining helpers it can call are fewer. This is already in effect today.

ai.title: SDK package.json cleanup and build script path fix
ai.summary: Removed redundant `access` and `typings` fields from `@codebuff/sdk` package.json. Added `typesVersions` mapping to support subpath type resolution. Moved `build.ts` to `scripts/` and updated the `build` script path. Removed `prepublishOnly` script, relying on `prepack` for build execution.

eli5.text: The package that developers use to build with Codebuff has had some tidy-up work done behind the scenes, cleaning out redundant settings in its configuration file and reorganizing a build helper into a dedicated folder for better organization. If you looked at the setup, you'd see that the build process now points to the new location of that helper, the configuration file is leaner with fewer overlapping entries, and a now-unnecessary duplicate build trigger has been removed in favor of a single, cleaner one. These changes streamline how the package is maintained and published, but don't alter what developers can actually do with it.

ai.title: SDK 0.2.2 adds ws dependency
ai.summary: SDK bumped to 0.2.2. Added ws 8.18.0 to runtime dependencies in sdk/package.json. Build script externalizes ws plus related Node modules (bufferutil, utf-8-validate, http, https, net, tls, url, events) in sdk/scripts/build.ts.

eli5.text: The Codebuff software kit now supports real-time communication, which lets programs exchange messages instantly instead of taking turns. This update affects developers who build tools on top of Codebuff's AI coding agent, enabling them to maintain live connections and receive immediate feedback during tasks. If you were using the kit to build such integrations, you may notice your applications can now handle continuous, two-way data streams without manual refreshes or polling.
